text: Two projectiles are thrown with same initial velocity making an angle of $45^{\circ }$ and  $30^{\circ }$ with the horizontal respectively. The ratio of their respective ranges will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here's how to determine the ratio of the ranges for the two projectiles:

Understanding the Concepts

Projectile Motion:  Projectile motion is the motion of an object thrown or projected into the air, subject to only the acceleration of gravity. The object is called a projectile, and its path is called its trajectory.

Range: The range of a projectile is the horizontal distance it covers from its launch point to the point where it returns to the same vertical height.

Key Formula

The formula for the range (R) of a projectile is:

$R=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g}$

where:

 R = Range

 u = Initial velocity (same for both projectiles)

 θ = Angle of projection

 g = Acceleration due to gravity (constant)

Calculations

Projectile 1 (45° angle):

Let the range of the projectile launched at 45° be $R_{1}$.

$R_{1}=\frac{u^{2}\sin (2\times 45^{\circ })}{g}=\frac{u^{2}\sin 90^{\circ }}{g}=\frac{u^{2}}{g}$

Projectile 2 (30° angle):

Let the range of the projectile launched at 30° be $R_{2}$.

$R_{2}=\frac{u^{2}\sin (2\times 30^{\circ })}{g}=\frac{u^{2}\sin 60^{\circ }}{g}=\frac{u^{2}\sqrt{3}}{2g}$

Ratio of Ranges $(R_{1}$ : $R_{2})$:

Divide the range of projectile 1 by the range of projectile 2:

$\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{\frac{u2}{g}}{\frac{u2\sqrt{3}}{2g}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$

To simplify the ratio, multiply both numerator and denominator by √3:

$\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}\times \sqrt{3}}{3\times \sqrt{3}}=\frac{6}{3\sqrt{3}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

Therefore, the ratio of the ranges of the two projectiles is 2 : √3, which corresponds to Option C.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: In a Vernier Calipers, 10 divisions of Vernier scale are equal to the 9 divisions of main scale. When both jaws of Vernier calipers touch each other, the zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the left of zero of the main scale and $4^{\text{th}}$ Vernier scale division exactly coincides with the main scale reading. One main scale division is equal to $1\mathrm{mm}$. While measuring diameter of a spherical body, the body is held between two jaws. It is now observed that zero of the Vernier scale lies between 30 and 31 divisions of main scale reading and $6^{\text{th}}$ Vernier scale division exactly coincides with the main scale reading. The diameter of the spherical body will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, In Vernier calipers, 10 VSD $=9$ MSD

$\Rightarrow \quad 1$ VSD $=\frac{9}{10}$ MSD

$\therefore$ Least count of vernier scale,

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{LC} & =1\mathrm{MSD}-1\mathrm{VSD} \\  \\ =1\mathrm{MSD}-\dfrac{9}{10}\mathrm{MSD}=\mathrm{MSD}\left (1-\dfrac{9}{10}\right ) \\  \\ =\dfrac{\text{MSD}}{10}=\dfrac{1\mathrm{mm}}{10}[\because 1\mathrm{MSD}=1\mathrm{mm}] \\  \\ =0.1\mathrm{mm}=0.01\mathrm{cm} \end{array}$

According to given situation,

Negative error $=$ Main scale reading - Least count $\times$

Number of coinciding main scale division

$=0.1-0.01\times 4=0.1-0.04=0.06\mathrm{cm}$

$\therefore$ Diameter of spherical body

$\begin{array}{l} =30\times 0.1+6\times 0.01+0.06 \\  \\ =3.0+0.06+0.06=3.12\mathrm{cm} \end{array}$

Which is closest to $3.10\mathrm{cm}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
The oscillating magnetic field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by 

$B_{y}=5\times 10^{-6}\sin 1000π\left (5x-4\times 10^{8}t\right )T$. The amplitude of electric field will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an electromagnetic wave, the magnitude of the electric field (E) and the magnetic field (B) are related by the speed of the wave (v), which can be represented as :

$E=Bv$

Here, B is the magnetic field, E is the electric field, and v is the speed of the electromagnetic wave. 

In the given problem, the peak value of the magnetic field is given as :

$B_{0}=5\times 10^{-6}T$

The wave speed (v) can be calculated from the given equation for the magnetic field, using the relationship between frequency (f), wave number (k), and speed :

$v=\frac{ω}{k}=\frac{1000π\times 4\times 10^{8}}{1000π\times 5}=8\times 10^{7}m/s$

Substituting these values into the equation for the electric field gives the peak value of the electric field :

$E_{0}=B_{0}v=5\times 10^{-6}T\times 8\times 10^{7}m/s=4\times 10^{2}V/m$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
A body is projected vertically upwards from the surface of earth with a velocity equal to one third of escape velocity. The maximum height attained by the body will be :

(Take radius of earth $=6400\mathrm{km}$ and $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Applying conservation of energy

$-\frac{GM_{e}m}{R_{e}}+\frac{1}{2}m\left (\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2Gm_{e}}{R_{e}}}\right )^{2}=-\frac{GM_{e}m}{R_{e}+h}$

$-\frac{GM_{e}m}{R_{e}}+\frac{GM_{e}m}{9R_{e}}=-\frac{GM_{e}m}{R_{e}+h}$

$\frac{8}{9R_{e}}=\frac{1}{R_{e}+h}$

$\Rightarrow h=\frac{R_{e}}{8}=\frac{6400}{8}=800$ km

text: A nucleus of mass $M$ at rest splits into two parts having masses $\frac{M^{'}}{3}$ and $\frac{2M^{'}}{3}(M^{'}<M)$. The ratio of de Broglie wavelength of two parts will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The nucleus is initially at rest, so its total momentum is zero; by conservation of linear momentum the two fragments move in opposite directions with equal momentum magnitudes, $p_{1}=p_{2}$.

The de Broglie wavelength $λ=\dfrac{h}{p}$ depends only on the momentum, so

$\dfrac{λ_{1}}{λ_{2}}=\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=1$

The masses $\dfrac{M^{'}}{3}$ and $\dfrac{2M^{'}}{3}$ only make the speeds differ ($v_{1}=2v_{2}$); the momenta, and hence the wavelengths, are equal.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
An ice cube of dimensions $60\mathrm{cm}\times 50\mathrm{cm}\times 20\mathrm{cm}$ is placed in an insulation box of wall thickness $1\mathrm{cm}$. The box keeping the ice cube at $0^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ of temperature is brought to a room of temperature $40^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The rate of melting of ice is approximately :

(Latent heat of fusion of ice is $3.4\times 10^{5}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{kg}^{-1}$ and thermal conducting of insulation wall is $0.05\mathrm{Wm}^{-1\circ }\mathrm{C}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Heat from the room reaches the ice through all six walls of the box, each of thickness $l=1\text{cm}=0.01\text{m}$. The area of the walls is the surface area of the ice block:

$A=2(0.6\times 0.5+0.5\times 0.2+0.6\times 0.2)=2(0.30+0.10+0.12)=1.04\text{m}^{2}$

With $k=0.05\text{W m}^{-1}{}^{\circ }\text{C}^{-1}$ and $\Delta T=40-0=40^{\circ }\text{C}$, the rate of heat flow is

$\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=\dfrac{kA\Delta T}{l}=\dfrac{0.05\times 1.04\times 40}{0.01}=208\text{W}$

This heat melts ice at $0^{\circ }\text{C}$, so $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=L\dfrac{dm}{dt}$:

$\dfrac{dm}{dt}=\dfrac{208}{3.4\times 10^{5}}\approx 6.1\times 10^{-4}\text{kg s}^{-1}=61\times 10^{-5}\text{kg s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: A transverse wave is represented by $y=2\sin (ωt-kx)\mathrm{cm}$. The value of wavelength (in $\mathrm{cm}$) for which the wave velocity becomes equal to the maximum particle velocity, will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $y=A\sin (ωt-kx)$ with $A=2\text{cm}$, the wave velocity is $v=\dfrac{ω}{k}$ and the particle velocity $\dfrac{𝜕y}{𝜕t}=Aω\cos (ωt-kx)$ has maximum value $Aω$.

Setting them equal,

$\dfrac{ω}{k}=Aω\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{1}{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}\text{cm}^{-1}$

$λ=\dfrac{2π}{k}=2π\times 2=4π\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
A source of potential difference $V$ is connected to the combination of two identical capacitors as shown in the figure. When key '$K$' is closed, the total energy stored across the combination is $E_{1}$. Now key '$K$' is opened and dielectric of dielectric constant 5 is introduced between the plates of the capacitors. The total energy stored across the combination is now $E_{2}$. The ratio $E_{1}/E_{2}$ will be :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the figure one capacitor is joined directly across the source and the other is joined through the key K.

With K closed, both capacitors are in parallel across $V$:

$E_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}(2C)V^{2}=CV^{2}$

When K is opened, the capacitor in the branch of K is isolated and keeps its charge $Q=CV$, while the other remains connected to the source and keeps the potential difference $V$. With the dielectric (constant 5) each capacitance becomes $5C$.

Capacitor still connected to the source: $\dfrac{1}{2}(5C)V^{2}=\dfrac{5}{2}CV^{2}$

Isolated capacitor: $\dfrac{Q^{2}}{2(5C)}=\dfrac{C^{2}V^{2}}{10C}=\dfrac{1}{10}CV^{2}$

$E_{2}=\dfrac{5}{2}CV^{2}+\dfrac{1}{10}CV^{2}=\dfrac{13}{5}CV^{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{E_{1}}{E_{2}}=\dfrac{5}{13}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
The area of cross section of the rope used to lift a load by a crane is $2.5\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The maximum lifting capacity of the crane is 10 metric tons. To increase the lifting capacity of the crane to 25 metric tons, the required area of cross section of the rope should be :

(take $g=10ms^{-2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The relationship between stress (σ), force (F), and area (A) is given by :

$σ=\frac{F}{A}$

In this context, the force is equal to the weight of the load, so we can substitute force with mass (m) times gravity (g) :

$F=m\cdot g$

From this, we get the formula for the cross-sectional area required to support a given mass :

$A=\frac{F}{σ}=\frac{m\cdot g}{σ}$

We can set up a proportionality relationship between the area for 10 metric tons (A₁₀) and the area for 25 metric tons (A₂₅) as follows :

$\frac{A_{10}}{A_{25}}=\frac{m_{10}}{m_{25}}$

Using the given values :

$A_{10}=2.5\times 10^{-4}$ m²,
$m_{10}=10,000$ kg,
$m_{25}=25,000$ kg,

Solving for $A_{25}$ :

$A_{25}=A_{10}\times \left (\frac{m_{25}}{m_{10}}\right )=2.5\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}\times \left (\frac{25,000\mathrm{kg}}{10,000\mathrm{kg}}\right )=6.25\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

So, Option A $(6.25\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2})$ is the correct answer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
In the given figure, the face $AC$ of the equilateral prism is immersed in a liquid of refractive index '$n$'. For incident angle $60^{\circ }$ at the side $AC$, the refracted light beam just grazes along face $AC$. The refractive index of the liquid $n=\frac{\sqrt{x}}{4}$. The value of $x$ is $____________$.

(Given refractive index of glass $=1.5$ )


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given prism is equilateral so, angle of prism, A $=60^{\circ }$

On first surface light is passing straight without any deviation, hence angle of refraction $\mathrm{r}_{1}=0^{\circ }$.

$\begin{array}{l} r_{1}+i_{2}=\mathrm{A} \\  \\ 0+i_{2}=60^{\circ } \\  \\ \Rightarrow i_{2}=60^{\circ } \end{array}$

On $2^{\text{nd}}$ surface ray, refracting ray is becoming parallel to the junction of surfaces, so $i_{2}$ will act as critical angle.

From snell's law $μ_{1}\sin θ_{1}=μ_{2}\sin θ_{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{3}{2}\sin i_{2}=μ\sin θ_{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow μ=\dfrac{3}{2}\times \dfrac{\sin 60^{\circ }}{\sin 90^{\circ }}=\dfrac{3}{2}\times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}\text{or}\dfrac{\sqrt{27}}{4} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$ Comparing above equation with 

given $n=\frac{\sqrt{x}}{4}$, we get $x=27$

text:
A uniform heavy rod of mass $20\mathrm{kg}$, cross sectional area $0.4\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and length $20\mathrm{m}$ is hanging from a fixed support. Neglecting the lateral contraction, the elongation in the rod due to its own weight is $x\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m}$. The value of $x$ is $_______________$.

(Given, young modulus Y = 2 $\times$ $10^{11} Nm^{-2}$ and $g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At a height $y$ above the free lower end, the rod supports the weight of the part below it, so the tension there is

$T(y)=\dfrac{Mg}{L}y$

An element of length $dy$ at that height stretches by $\dfrac{T(y)\qquad dy}{AY}$, so the total elongation is

$\Delta L=\int\limits _{0}^{L}\dfrac{Mgy}{LAY}dy=\dfrac{MgL}{2AY}$

The factor 2 appears because the tension rises linearly from zero at the bottom to $Mg$ at the support, an average of $\dfrac{Mg}{2}$.

$\Delta L=\dfrac{20\times 10\times 20}{2\times 0.4\times 2\times 10^{11}}=\dfrac{4000}{1.6\times 10^{11}}=2.5\times 10^{-8}\text{m}=25\times 10^{-9}\text{m}$

Hence, the answer is 25.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: In a coil of resistance $8~\Omega$, the magnetic flux due to an external magnetic field varies with time as $𝜙=\frac{2}{3}\left (9-t^{2}\right )$. The value of total heat produced in the coil, till the flux becomes zero, will be $_____________$ $J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$R=8\Omega$

$𝜙=\frac{2}{3}(9-t^{2})$

At $t=3$, $𝜙=0$

$ε=\left |-\frac{d𝜙}{dt}\right |=\frac{4}{3}t$

$H=\int\limits _{0}^{3}\frac{V^{2}}{R}dt=\int\limits _{0}^{3}\frac{1}{8}\times \frac{16}{9}t^{2}dt$

$=\frac{2}{9}\times \left (\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right )_{0}^{3}=\frac{2}{9\times 3}\times 27=2J$

As per given figures, two springs of spring constants $k$ and $2k$ are connected to mass $m$. If the period of oscillation in figure (a) is $3\mathrm{s}$, then the period of oscillation in figure (b) will be $\sqrt{x}s$. The value of $x$ is $___________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For case (a),

$K_{eq}=\frac{2K}{3}$

For case (b),

$K_{eq}=3K$

$\because$ $T=2π\sqrt{\frac{m}{K}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{T_{a}}{T_{b}}=\sqrt{\frac{K_{b}}{K_{a}}}$

$\frac{3}{T_{b}}=\sqrt{\frac{3K\times 3}{2K}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$

$T_{b}=\sqrt{2}$

$x=2$
